jobs.title: Structures and Chassis CAE Engineer - GM Defense
jobs.location: 2 Locations
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 The Role 
 The Structures and Chassis CAE Engineer supports GM Defense by applying finite element analysis tools and methods to the design and development of body structure, RESS structure, chassis structure, suspension, steering components, and other vehicle structures. This role leads analysis activities that assess strength, static and dynamic stiffness, durability, and noise and vibration performance, and translates results into clear design recommendations.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Perform CAE analyses to support vehicle program execution and technology development across structural systems.
 Support component and subsystem test development, root cause analysis, and issue resolution.
 Perform fatigue analysis and develop block cycles used to drive physical testing for chassis, suspension, RESS, and related structural components.
 Create, document, and archive analysis models and results.
 Present results and provide actionable recommendations to support virtual reviews and program decision-making.
 Participate in Chassis Structure, Suspension, Steering, Structures Product Development, Vehicle Dynamics, and Noise and Vibration Performance Integration teams.
 Work closely with design engineers to develop new components and subsystems, define system requirements, and deliver technical solutions for current and future programs.
 Lead coordinated supplier CAE activities and support the Statement of Requirements process.
 Develop, maintain, and update the CAE portions of analysis, development, and validation plans.
 Provide technical leadership for advanced technology development, contribute to new CAE methods and techniques, and stay current with emerging tools, trends, and competitive products.
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Engineering, or Physics.
 5+ years of related experience in product design and the CAE field.
 Experience mentoring others and providing technical leadership in a CAE-focused environment.
 Familiarity with optimization, DOE, and automation of CAE workflows using tools such as Python, Tcl/Tk, AI/ML or similar to enable efficiency, automate repetitive tasks, and drive rapid product development.
 Strong knowledge of engineering fundamentals relevant to the role, such as mechanics, physics, metallurgy, manufacturing methods, electronics, software, or control systems.
 Experience with CAE modeling tools such as HyperWorks and/or ANSA.
 Experience with linear and non-linear CAE analysis tools such as NASTRAN, OptiStruct, Abaqus, LS-DYNA, and/or Adams.
 Experience with structural fatigue theory, tools, and methods, including DesignLife and/or nCode.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, sound analytical judgment, and the ability to solve complex, ambiguous problems while working effectively across teams.
 Candidate must either be a U.S. Person (U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, asylee or refugee) or a non-U.S. Person who is eligible to obtain any required export control authorization. 
 
 What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 
 Master’s degree in Engineering
 Engineering design and release experience
 Optimization integration into product design and development
 Previous Defense industry experience

jobs.title: Senior State Estimation Engineer
jobs.location: 3 Locations
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.  
 
 Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.
 
 About the Role: 
 
 As a Senior State Estimation Engineer within the SEAM Embodied AI organization, you will be a senior individual contributor driving cutting-edge sensor calibration and state estimation solutions that directly impact autonomous driving performance. Your role is pivotal in designing, architecting, and deploying advanced systems for purposes including pinpointing the vehicle’s location in the world, and calibrating parameters of all sensors to ensure they optimally support many other vehicle subsystems. You'll lead critical technical initiatives, collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, mentor engineers across the organization, and significantly shape the future of onboard autonomous driving capabilities.  
 
 About the Organization: 
 
 The SEAM Embodied AI team is at the forefront of developing groundbreaking sensor fusion systems powering fully autonomous vehicles. We leverage modern approaches that are both practical and theoretically sound, supported with top quality code and rigorous testing. Our solutions enable robust state estimation for the purposes of real-time localization, static and dynamic sensor calibration, as well as onboard and offboard high-fidelity map creation at scale. Join a collaborative and innovative team redefining autonomy through state-of-the-art methodology, delivering solutions that move beyond current technological boundaries.  
   
 What You'll Do:   
 Drive the design, development, and deployment of advanced solutions for state estimation, localization, sensor calibration and more.  

 Lead and architect complex projects, from conception through validation to onboard implementation, emphasizing scalability, robustness, and safety-critical operation.  

 Champion innovation in multi-sensor self-calibration in unstructured environments, state estimation architectures, and fault tolerance strategies suited for real-time onboard deployment.  

 Provide technical mentorship and thought leadership, elevating engineering practices, and fostering innovation across teams.  

 Collaborate closely with multidisciplinary engineering groups, ensuring seamless integration of localization, sensor alignment, and other capabilities into autonomous vehicle systems.  

 Influence technical roadmaps, shaping strategic priorities aligned with company objectives and product milestones.  

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)   
 Bachelors Degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.  

 3+ years or relevant industry experience

 At least 3 years of extensive experience developing and deploying advanced state estimation and/or sensor calibration systems, particularly in real-time onboard applications.  

 Proven track record as a technical leader and expert in sensor calibration, state estimation, and/or localization, operating on a wide variety of sensor inputs to perform robustly within safety-critical systems.  

 Strong software engineering proficiency, particularly in C++ and Python, alongside extensive hands-on experience with development, integration, and testing tools. 

 Excellent communication, collaboration, and mentoring abilities, comfortable influencing technical strategy and guiding engineering excellence across the organization.  

What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) : 
 AV/ADAS experience is a big plus 

 Masters or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

 At least 5 years of extensive experience developing and deploying advanced state estimation and/or sensor calibration systems, particularly in real-time onboard applications.

jobs.title: Interior Vehicle Systems Engineer (VSE)
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 The Interior Vehicle Systems Engineer (VSE) serves as the SMT functional leader and Chief Engineer for a vehicle program. This role owns Interior design intent and technical execution, ensuring subsystem decisions align with vehicle-level performance, quality, timing, and cost targets while managing complex subsystem, system, and vehicle integration at the SMT level. The VSE leads a diverse, global team of engineers, with input from Studio, Manufacturing, Compartment Integration, Program Planning, Validation, Specifications, Suppliers, and Purchasing, to execute high-quality designs, overcome unique challenges, and enable program goals while providing managerial leadership to keep the program on time, within budget, and delivered with quality.

 The VSE is the single voice of the designated program. Success in this role requires strong technical leadership, program management and planning, and the ability to influence across a complex organization to deliver results. They will be an effective communicator and team leader who can perceive and analyze risk, work to mitigate risk early, think ahead and plan several steps into the future, prioritize and manage multiple challenges concurrently, break down roadblocks, and challenge the status quo when appropriate.

 What You’ll Do (Responsibilities): 
 System Integration & Program Leadership
 Own Interior coordination across systems, subsystems, and vehicle interfaces; balance interior content & technical imperatives aligned to program targets and milestones. Drive engineering execution efficiency, strategically planning SMT engagement on the most critical program risks.
 
 Technical Leadership
 Lead structured problem solving, root-cause analysis, and trade-off decisions; define must-be-true conditions, set constraints, and make timely decisions to protect Interior imperatives.
 Identify and resolve Interior issues at both component and vehicle levels; balance customer experience, craftsmanship, manufacturability, cost, safety, and enterprise constraints through clear technical communication.
 Remain highly program-focused on implementation, acting as the primary contact for the program team and SMT leaders.
 
 Executive & Cross-Functional Communication
 Deliver concise, executive-ready updates (written, verbal, and visual); prioritize and tailor information for leaders, Design Release Engineers, Engineering Group Managers, Studio, and functional partners.
 
 Influence, Negotiation & Alignment
 Align stakeholders with competing objectives across Studio, Engineering, Performance, Manufacturing, and Program Teams; remove enterprise-level roadblocks and secure cross-functional agreement on Interior content and design.
 
 Program Management & Planning
 Develop and manage Interior 30/60/90-day and long-range plans; appropriately push back on scope; delegate effectively; identify and mitigate Interior system risks early.
 Lead Interior Engineering’s delivery against imperative targets along the develop development process glidepath; synthesize detailed Interior inputs into aggregate status.
 Drive Interior program deliverables, benchmarking, cost management, human factors, interface requirements, craftsmanship, and financial/quality imperatives; co-lead supplier selection, tooling kick-off, and production tooling readiness.
 Lead vehicle-level integration execution across functional leaders, ensuring alignment with prior advanced strategies.
 Troubleshoot integration conflicts and system-level execution gaps, escalating key launch issues and coordinating critical launch-issue mobilization efforts.
 Anticipate risk, lead Interior engineering changes, and coordinate validation activities; support release engineers, issue resolution teams, and plant teams through development, build events, and vehicle launch.
 Develop a support network for critical launch issues with cross-functional teams to drive rapid resolution. Ensure cross-functional alignment for launch excellence, escalating high-impact issues to key leadership forums.
 Champion engineering with simplicity through simplification, standardization, and shared execution strategies; develop and communicate a pipeline of Interior SMT efficiency ideas.
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 
 Bachelor’s degree (BSE or BS) in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Chemistry, Metallurgical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Physics, or Materials Engineering.
 5+ years of engineering experience.
 Experience in interior engineering.
 Ability to travel during vehicle launches.
 
 What Can Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): 
 Knowledge of GM processes and strategies.
 Experience leading interior system releases across multiple interior commodities and programs.
 Demonstrated understanding of interior architecture, subsystem integration, and vehicle-level integration.
 Experience making and communicating vehicle-level trade-off decisions within cross-functional program teams.
 Experience with Studio Integration and Color, Materials, and Finish (CMF), including the ability to translate creative direction and craftsmanship expectations into executable technical decisions.
 Proven ability to balance content, design intent, engineering execution, manufacturing needs, customer experience, timing, cost, quality, validation, and vehicle performance.
 Deep understanding of the interdependencies within the vehicle development process.
 Proven ability to identify, assess, and mitigate risk; elevate issues appropriately; and mobilize the right resources at the right time.
 Experience supporting programs from strategy and execution through builds, issue resolution, and launch.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Rendering Infrastructure (AV Simulation)
jobs.location: Sunnyvale, California, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Role Overview
 As a Senior Software Engineer on the Rendering Infrastructure team, you will build the systems that turn a GPU-accelerated, physically-based sensor simulator into a production platform — one that runs reproducibly, at cluster scale, and against production-representative autonomous vehicle interfaces. This is a systems role at the boundary of rendering, simulation, perception, and distributed infrastructure. You will connect the renderer to AV software stacks and compute clusters, reproduce real sensor scheduling and vehicle timing, run many worlds concurrently on a single GPU, and make the runtime start fast and stay cheap across thousands of workers. Your work determines whether closed-loop simulation — the vehicle software in the loop with the renderer, not just offline synthetic data generation — is trustworthy and affordable: whether a run reproduces, whether synthetic sensor feeds arrive with the same timing quirks the real vehicle sees, and how many scenarios we can execute per GPU-hour. We build in modern C++ and Python on Linux, with ROS, PyTorch, CUDA, NVIDIA OptiX, NVIDIA MDL, and OpenUSD. We're looking for someone who enjoys this layer — debugging nondeterminism across a process boundary, cutting cold-start time by changing how a runtime is packaged, and reasoning about GPU memory and IPC in the same conversation.
 
 About the Team
 The Rendering Infrastructure team owns the foundational systems the broader Rendering team builds on top of: asset and scene ingestion, GPU memory and resource management, acceleration structure construction, packaging and deployment, profiling infrastructure, and the core engine abstractions of our physically-based sensor simulation system. We also own how the renderer connects to the AV stack and world simulator, as a library or a service, and how consumers configure it — what it produces, at what fidelity, and how it behaves when something goes wrong. We sit between the rendering algorithms team and everyone who consumes simulated sensor data — perception training, closed-loop validation and reinforcement learning. We care about determinism, throughput per GPU, iteration speed, and infrastructure that stays comprehensible as it scales.
 
 Why Join Us?
 Work on hard systems problems with an unusually clear definition of success — reproducibility, timing fidelity, frames per second per GPU, and worker spin-up time are all measurable, and all of them matter. Own meaningful surface area: the AV stack integration and transport layer, the sensor scheduling and timing model, multi-world rendering on a single GPU, or the runtime deployment and asset delivery path, depending on your strengths. Sit at the center of the simulation stack, where rendering, perception, and infrastructure meet, and see your work used across the organization for perception training, closed-loop simulation, and reinforcement learning. Join a team that pairs rigor — design documents, reproducibility, profiling, and regression testing — with pragmatic engineering and short feedback loops.
 
 What You'll Do
 You will own one or more of the following areas and contribute across the others, depending on your strengths and team priorities.
 Connect the renderer to AV software stacks and compute clusters — designing low-latency, high-bandwidth transport using ROS/ROS 2, shared-memory IPC, gRPC, and sockets with appropriate serialization formats, and streaming multi-sensor payloads into the autonomous vehicle stack.
 Integrate the renderer with learned driving models through Gymnasium-style environment APIs — stepping the simulation from Python, exchanging observations and actions efficiently with PyTorch-based models, and preserving deterministic execution while minimizing per-step overhead for eval and training at scale.
 Integrate the runtime with the cloud and on-premises execution environments used for large-scale closed-loop testing, continuous integration, and perception training pipelines.
 Improve and validate deterministic execution — establishing the required bit-accurate or frame-deterministic lock-step behavior across the simulation clock, dynamic physics updates, and the ray-traced renderer, and building the tooling that demonstrates a run reproduces to the agreed bar.
 Reproduce real sensor scheduling and vehicle timing — staggered camera exposures, rolling shutter behavior, LiDAR spin and packet rates, hardware clock drift, and the onboard constraints perception actually operates under, including P95/P99 compute latency, transport lag, and packet drops.
 Build perturbation mechanisms that inject timing jitter, dropped or out-of-order frames, and calibration drift in both extrinsics and intrinsics, and use them to stress-test downstream perception and sensor fusion robustness in closed-loop runs.
 Build memory-efficient multi-world and multi-scenario execution inside a single rendering process, using shared geometry and instancing — OptiX IAS/GAS, or the analogous acceleration structure hierarchies in Vulkan/DXR — so concurrent rollouts share static map geometry instead of duplicating it in GPU memory.
 Optimize GPU memory footprint, scene streaming, and execution scheduling to maximize frames per second per GPU across concurrent simulation workers.
 Improve runtime deployment and asset delivery — deterministic deployment packages (SquashFS archives, read-only container layers, memory-mapped storage) and low-overhead loaders for OpenUSD scene graphs and NVIDIA MDL materials that work against compressed, read-only filesystems without redundant decompression or copies.
 Build distributed caches for textures, precompiled OptiX/PTX shader pipelines, and prebuilt acceleration structures to eliminate cold-start compilation and redundant I/O at cluster scale.
 Profile and reduce disk, network, and memory footprints to cut worker spin-up time, binary payload size, and asset ingestion overhead.
 Partner with the 3D content and USD pipeline teams to set runtime budgets, automated validation rules, and compression workflows before assets enter deployment.
 Uphold high standards through technical design documents, code review, reproducibility and performance regression testing, and mentorship of other engineers.
 
 What You Must Have
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a substantial portion focused on performance-critical systems software.
 Production proficiency in modern C++ (C++17/20), including performance optimization, memory management, and clean API and system design in a large codebase, plus working proficiency in Python for tooling and automation.
 Strong Linux systems programming foundation: multithreading and concurrency, memory management, IPC, and high-throughput data movement, including systems that operate across process and machine boundaries.
 Depth in at least one of the two domains this role bridges, and the interest to grow into the other: Robotics or autonomous systems — the architecture and integration of perception, planning, or control components, and experience with at least one interface those systems are driven through: real-time middleware (ROS/ROS 2, DDS, custom IPC, or high-rate publish/subscribe) and / or a Gymnasium-style environment API; or

GPU programming through a compute or ray tracing API (CUDA, OptiX, Vulkan, DXR, or similar), with a working understanding of GPU memory and execution models.
 
 A track record of designing, implementing, and debugging reliable distributed systems, including the nondeterminism and failure modes that come with them.
 Experience profiling and optimizing real systems, and the instinct to measure before optimizing.
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across rendering, simulation, perception, infrastructure, and content pipeline teams.
 
 Bonus Points
 Experience in one or more of the following is helpful; we do not expect any candidate to have all of it.
 Working knowledge of how autonomous driving perception stacks ingest sensor feeds — sensor scheduling, staggered exposures, rolling shutter, LiDAR packet rates, and onboard compute and transport latency budgets.
 Experience designing closed-loop simulation edge cases and perturbations: schedule jitter, dropped frames, out-of-order packets, and calibration or extrinsics drift.
 Experience with batched rendering, multi-viewport rendering, or multi-scenario execution on a single GPU using acceleration structure hierarchies and instancing (OptiX IAS/GAS, Vulkan/DXR TLAS/BLAS).
 Strength in both domains above rather than one — GPU systems, and robotics or autonomous systems — or practical depth in ray tracing and path tracing specifically (NVIDIA OptiX, Vulkan Ray Tracing, or DirectX Raytracing). 

Hands-on Linux deployment optimization: SquashFS, loop devices, memory-mapped files, zero-copy loading, container overlay layers, and cold-start reduction across compute nodes.
 Experience designing high-performance texture and shader caching systems — OptiX disk cache, Vulkan pipeline cache, or PTX distribution.
 Experience consuming OpenUSD in a C++ runtime and optimizing stage traversal and runtime memory layout.
 Familiarity with deploying and scaling containerized simulation jobs on cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) or on-premises HPC clusters.
 Exposure to autonomous vehicle or robotics simulation platforms such as NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac Sim, DRIVE Sim, Unreal Engine, or custom in-house simulators.
 Experience supporting reinforcement learning environments or Gymnasium-style simulation interfaces as downstream consumers.
 Evidence of technical contribution through open-source rendering, simulation, or systems infrastructure work, internal platforms, publications, or other knowledge sharing.
 
 Candidate Profile
 Relevant experience may come from robotics, perception, simulation, rendering and graphics, game engines, HPC, or distributed systems infrastructure. Direct autonomous vehicle experience is not required. Successful candidates will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with practical intuition for sensor data, simulation timing, GPU execution, and distributed runtime environments.
 
 Compensation
 The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of New York, Colorado, California, or Washington.
 The salary range for this role is $153,200 to $234,100. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.
 Bonus Potential: An incentive pay program offers payouts based on company performance, job level, and individual performance.
 
 Benefits
 GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays, tuition assistance programs, employee assistance program, GM vehicle discounts and more.
 
 Hybrid/Remote
 This role can be based remotely.
 
 *This job may be eligible for relocation benefits if you are interested in relocating to the Bay Area.

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 The Role 

 GM Defense is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Chassis Design Engineer to lead suspension system development for defense vehicles. In this role, you will provide engineering leadership across the full product lifecycle—from concept development and design through validation, production readiness, and launch—while ensuring suspension systems meet performance, durability, safety, compliance, and mission requirements.

 What You'll Do 

 You’ll lead suspension system development from concept through production, translating vehicle-level performance, durability, safety, and mission requirements into robust component and assembly designs. Working with cross-functional engineering teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you’ll mature designs, resolve issues, and keep component delivery on track.

 As the program progresses, you’ll guide analysis and validation, support PTB, APPV/PPV, and NS/S builds, and manage engineering changes through launch. You’ll use CAE, TcVis, field data, and program KPIs to identify risks and opportunities, make informed trade-offs, and drive continuous improvement. You’ll also serve as a technical leader by mentoring junior engineers and helping the team deliver safe, compliant, and production-ready suspension systems.

 Analyze warranty and field data to identify and address design issues and opportunities for improvement.
 Apply DFMEA, DRBFM, and DFSS methodologies to ensure robust design and manufacturing processes.
 Apply GD&T and tolerance analysis principles to critical component and assembly designs.
 Apply structured problem-solving techniques to complex engineering challenges.
 Benchmark competitive designs and technologies to drive innovation and best practices.
 Demonstrates rapid proficiency in new technologies and engineering tools.
 Design components that support vehicle performance, durability, and safety requirements.
 Develop and manage engineering specifications, requirements, and validation plans.
 Manage component delivery across the product lifecycle, collaborating with suppliers and manufacturing.
 Manage engineering changes and releases throughout the program phases.
 Manage safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements for all suspension system components.
 Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior engineers and cross-functional teams.
 Support PTB, APPV/PPV, NS/S build processes for system validation and production readiness.
 Use CAE and TcVis analysis to optimize designs, predict performance, and identify potential issues.
 Use engineering data and KPIs to track progress, make informed decisions, and drive continuous improvement.
   
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) 

 10+ years of experience in chassis and suspension system design and development.
 Proficiency in applying DFMEA, DRBFM, and DFSS.
 Demonstrated ability to apply structured problem-solving techniques.
 Ability to rapidly learn and apply new technologies.
 Proven ability to design robust and compliant components.
 Strong project management skills, including component delivery and engineering change management.
 Familiarity with safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements in automotive or defense industries.
 Proven technical leadership and mentoring capabilities.
 Candidate must be a U.S. Person (U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, asylee or refugee). 
  
 What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 

 Expertise in GD&T and tolerance analysis.
 Experience benchmarking competitive designs.
 Experience in developing and managing engineering specifications and validation plans.
 Experience with PTB, APPV/PPV and NS/S processes.
 Proficient in CAE and TcVis analysis tools.
 Ability to utilize engineering data and KPIs for decision-making.

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 The Role:    
 At AV (Autonomous Vehicles) Software Organization within General Motors, we are working on developing cutting-edge ADAS and AV features for next-generation vehicles.  
 
 As the ADAS/AV Platform Software Verification Engineer, you will play a crucial role in defining, implementing, and optimizing system testing to ensure the quality, safety, and reliability of the ADAS platform software. 
  
 Responsibilities: 
 Design and develop scalable, high-coverage software testing for the ADAS/AV platform. 

 Analyze diagnostics from a full-vehicle perspective to support efficient triaging and debugging related to ADAS/AV Platform Software. 

 Build and Maintain hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), software-in-the-loop (SIL), and vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) testing environments.

 Ensure compliance with legal standards and safety requirements, including ISO 26262, SOTIF, FMVSS 111, and FMVSS 127, while improving test coverage and metrics. 

 Collaborate with Software Infra and application teams to develop new test cases, leveraging expertise in Service-Oriented Architecture, Middleware communication (Pub Sub/DDS/Subspace), diagnostics, Linux and QNX. 

 Work closely with Software Development and Hardware teams to debug and root-cause issues within Linux/QNX-based ADAS/AV Platform Software. 

 Create Test automation frameworks, develop test scripts, and execute automated tests to enhance validation efficiency. 

 Conduct and assist with test result analysis, including FMEA, Root Cause Analysis (Ishikawa/Fishbone Analysis, A-B-A Testing). 

 Assist in issue triaging, log analysis, and troubleshooting ADAS/AV Platform issues. 

 Required Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's degree in electronics, computer science, electrical engineering or a related technical degree

 Minimum of 6 years of professional technical experience

 Minimum of 3 years of working experience in Software Verification and Validation. 

 Strong Programming skills in Python, CAPL, Vehicle Spy and Robot Framework . 

 Good understanding of Vehicle networks like CAN and Ethernet.  

 Knowledge of network analysis and debugging tools, Ex: Wireshark, CANoe/CANalyzer, INCA, RAD Galaxy RAD Gigastar.  

 Ability to understand the requirements and transfer that into Test Scenarios, Situations / Tests, or testable scripts to be used in vehicle simulation environments. 

 Flexible, dependable, self-initiative, and capable of learning new skills and technologies.

 Possess a valid driver’s license and the ability to operate test vehicles  

 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Must have hands-on Experience with QNX or Linux based software systems and Embedded programming. 

 Knowledge in ROS, Linux-based embedded systems, and RTOS environments. 

 Excellent cross-collaboration and critical problem-solving skills. 

 Experience in Unified Diagnostic Services (ISO 14229), TCP and UDP . 

 Knowledge of automotive communication protocols (Ethernet, DDS, CAN, SOME/IP)

jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Work Arrangement: 
  
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Milford, Michigan three times per week, at minimum.
  
 The Role: 
  
 We are looking for a Controller System Integration Manager (CSIM) to join our Vehicle Mechatronics Embedded Controls (VMEC) organization! This Controller System Integration Manager is a challenging technical leadership position in the development, integration and launch of embedded controller products in all vehicles. 

 This Staff position is responsible for creating, communicating, and managing various types of ‘program’ plans and ensuring the on-time delivery of an embedded controller and/or its sub-components. In addition, you will lead the Daily Stand-Up meeting with key partners to ensure all requirements and tasks are met on-time with "world's best" quality. You will also lead and establish technical direction for both internal (GM) and external (supplier) engineering support personnel. This position includes frequent written and oral communication with executive leadership. 

 Lastly, this role contains a high level of cross-functional responsibility with limited formal authority, providing excellent opportunities for developing and honing the skill of influencing others.
  
 What You'll Do: 

 Ensure that the product development and release plans are created and executed in adherence to engineering standard work for the purpose of on-time high quality delivery of VMEC embedded control products.
 Identify and resolve any coordination issues between the calibration team, SW DRE, SWIM, SWIL, and Hardware DREs.
 Act as an integration manager and primary interface with customers (e.g., vehicle program teams or vehicle assembly plants) and development partners (e.g., calibration teams, validation teams, or suppliers) of the specific product of responsibility; includes tracking and reporting status of deliverables.
 Refine, Maintain, and Prioritize the team backlog.
 Lead or support standard meetings related to specific responsibilities (e.g., Daily stand-up Meeting or Software Execution Team Meeting).
 Provides technical leadership ensuring issue resolution and appropriate technical direction for products of responsibility.
 Escalate issues as required, for executive leadership support.
 Interface with Lead Calibrators and Technical Specialists to escalate SW needs as required.
 Lead system level corrective action teams (e.g., critical launch issues with calibration and software coordinated action).
 Own system-level PRTS through PRC to identify key issue owners.
 Train, coach, mentor other team members in areas of strong competency.
 Lead and support continuous process improvements, best practices, lessons learned, and quality improvement initiatives.
 Single point controller contact for Propulsion product teams: represent controller team at Core PDT, SMT and GPS PAPIR/PET/CPIT/PPDR.
 Overall PRTS leader for all assigned programs: support status review, forecast risk and work across teams and leadership levels to deliver program content with best quality.
  
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 

 Bachelor's degree in one of the following: Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or other equivalent engineering degrees.
 Minimum of 7 years of engineering/technical experience.
 Minimum of 7 years of experience in real-time embedded software system, such as controller hardware design, sensor and actuator design, algorithm design, software development, calibration, integration, testing and validation, electrical architecture design, etc.
 Minimum of 5 years of experience as a technical project lead or project manager with proven experience in accomplishing project deliverables and goals.
 Experience leading meetings.
 Demonstrated drive for results and teamwork in project execution.
 Demonstrated analytical ability where problems are unusual and difficult.
 Demonstrated proficiency in project management skills, especially within automotive product lifecycle.
 Demonstrated skill to deliver results in a complex and highly demanding development and production environment addressing multiple high-priority topics with success.
  
 What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Skills): 

 Master’s degree in engineering or computer Science or MBA.
 10+ years of automotive experience.
 Understanding of AUTOSAR software constructs and their implementation.
 Understanding of trouble shooting and root-causing vehicle issues.
 Understanding of vehicle architecture and Software Driven Vehicle concept.
 Understanding of automated software build and release process.

Note: program participants are required to purchase/lease a qualifying GM vehicle every four years unless one of a limited number of exceptions applies.

jobs.title: Autonomous Vehicle Test Engineer
jobs.location: Yuma, Arizona, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Position summary
 GM Level: 6A

 Proposed job-family alignment: Test and Validation Engineering

 Primary work location: GM Desert Proving Ground, Yuma, Arizona

 Travel: Approximately 10% as needed for training, team alignment, vehicle support, or other GM testing activities

 Career track: Individual contributor

General Motors is developing advanced driving-assistance and autonomous-vehicle capabilities that require safe, repeatable, and scalable validation. The AV Test Engineer will be the onsite technical lead for a focused closed-course testing operation at GM’s Desert Proving Ground in Yuma, Arizona.
 
 This role will own day-to-day technical execution for a small assigned fleet of approximately two to three autonomous test vehicles. The engineer will plan and execute closed-course regression, feature, behavior, calibration, and other structured testing; coordinate limited operations personnel supporting the work; and ensure the vehicles, test setup, track activities, data, and results are ready to support engineering and program decisions.
 
 Yuma is intentionally a lean operating environment. There will not be dedicated technicians or additional engineers permanently onsite to provide routine support. The successful candidate must be a self-starter who can operate independently, recognize and resolve common vehicle and AV-system issues, and know when to stop testing or escalate to remote engineering, Service Operations, Fleet Reliability Engineering, Vehicle Integration, or other partners. The role requires comfort moving between test planning, driving and observing closed-course scenarios, vehicle health checks, troubleshooting, data handling, and clear technical communication.
 
 The position is especially important during the winter testing season, when Yuma provides a weather-resilient location to maintain closed-course testing capacity when conditions or schedule constraints limit testing elsewhere. The engineer will help make the local fleet and facility a dependable, repeatable testing capability rather than a temporary campaign location.
 
 What you’ll do
 Lead onsite closed-course testing
 Serve as the onsite technical lead for all assigned AV closed-course testing activities at Yuma, translating approved test requests and engineering objectives into executable plans, procedures, schedules, and resource requirements.

 Plan and execute repeatable software regression, feature and behavior validation, structured scenario, calibration, fault-response, and targeted data-collection tests.

 Coordinate daily test sequencing, track reservations, vehicle assignments, operating windows, safety reviews, and test readiness with remote AV Test Engineering and cross-functional stakeholders.

 Direct and brief limited operations personnel supporting test execution, including task assignments, vehicle preparation, track setup, lead-vehicle or target support, run sequencing, communications, and post-run closeout.

 Provide clear technical direction during test execution while maintaining the distinction between engineering ownership and operations execution responsibilities.

 Make timely onsite decisions about whether a test is ready to proceed, should be modified, should be repeated, or must be stopped and escalated based on vehicle condition, system behavior, track conditions, weather, data quality, or safety risk.

 Support extended or non-standard testing schedules when required by release timing, track availability, seasonal priorities, or campaign needs, consistent with site and safety requirements.

 Own the assigned Yuma test fleet
 Act as the primary technical owner for approximately two to three assigned AV test vehicles, maintaining awareness of their configuration, software and calibration state, physical condition, instrumentation, data-recording readiness, and current availability.

 Perform or coordinate daily vehicle checkouts, pre-drive readiness checks, post-drive inspections, charging or fueling coordination, sensor and camera cleanliness checks, hard-drive or data-media handling, and other activities required to keep vehicles test-ready.

 Manage vehicle configuration and test preparation activities, including approved software or branch deployments, calibration updates, route or map selection, logging configuration, test tools, and required test assets.

 Maintain accurate vehicle status, mileage or test-hour records, configuration information, test history, open issues, and return-to-service decisions for the local fleet.

 Identify vehicle downtime risks early and develop practical containment, recovery, and escalation plans to protect testing availability.

 Coordinate parts, materials, shipping, facility resources, charging support, and remote technical assistance when onsite needs exceed available capability.

 Build and maintain a winter-readiness plan for the Yuma fleet, including vehicle availability, spare equipment, data-storage capacity, charging or fueling needs, test assets, operating procedures, and contingency plans.

 Troubleshoot vehicle and AV-system issues
 Perform first-line technical triage for issues involving the AV software stack, vehicle compute, sensors, localization, calibration, connectivity, data recording, host-vehicle systems, vehicle networks, power or charging, and test infrastructure.

 Use vehicle symptoms, operator observations, system status, logs, drive data, diagnostic tools, and repeatable experiments to isolate likely causes and determine the next action.

 Reproduce issues when safe and practical, capture accurate timelines and evidence, and create actionable issue reports for remote engineering or support teams.

 Distinguish between issues that can be safely contained or corrected onsite and issues requiring vehicle removal from service, engineering review, formal change control, or additional safety assessment.

 Partner with Troubleforce, Service Operations, Fleet Reliability Engineering, Vehicle Integration, AV software and hardware teams, and other remote experts to drive issues toward resolution.

 Support controlled fault-injection or non-nominal testing when requested, ensuring that test intent, expected system response, safety controls, and data-labeling requirements are understood before execution.

 Develop practical troubleshooting guides, recovery procedures, checklists, and escalation paths that reduce dependence on ad hoc support and improve repeatability for future Yuma personnel.

 Deliver high-quality test results and data
 Execute test procedures consistently and capture complete run information, including vehicle, software, calibration, map, track, scenario, operator, weather, and timing details.

 Evaluate AV behavior and system response against defined test objectives and acceptance criteria, distinguishing objective evidence from anecdotal observations.

 Capture and communicate pass, fail, blocked, incomplete, and inconclusive outcomes with enough context for engineering teams to act without repeating avoidable setup work.

 Ensure drive links, logs, hard drives or data media, notes, screenshots, issue references, and other required evidence are transferred or uploaded through approved workflows.

 Review test data for completeness, corruption, missing signals, unexpected configuration changes, or other conditions that could limit its usefulness.

 Publish concise test summaries and status updates to the appropriate engineering and operations forums, and maintain traceability in tools such as Jira, Confluence, Xray, Slack, and approved data or fleet-management systems.

 Provide timely feedback to remote software, systems, simulation, safety, and program teams so that test results support release decisions, feature refinement, and issue prioritization.

 Establish a dependable Yuma operating model
 Help stand up and continuously improve the permanent Yuma closed-course testing capability, including roles, standard work, readiness gates, communications, operating rhythms, and handoffs with the broader AV Test Engineering and AV Operations organizations.

 Maintain a repeatable intake-to-execution workflow for local test requests, including request clarification, prioritization, planning, execution, results reporting, and issue follow-up.

 Create and maintain onsite documentation for vehicle checkout, test preparation, track use, safety controls, data handling, troubleshooting, emergency response, and end-of-day closeout.

 Coordinate with DPG Site Operations, Safety, Infrastructure, Mapping, security, and other facility partners to ensure the local operation meets site requirements and has the resources needed to execute safely.

 Track local performance indicators such as vehicle availability, test hours, completed runs, blocked runs, downtime, repeat failures, data-upload timeliness, issue aging, and test-request cycle time.

 Identify opportunities to increase usable testing hours, reduce avoidable setup and reset time, improve vehicle utilization, and shift repeatable work to appropriately trained operations personnel.

 Capture lessons learned from winter testing and other campaigns and convert them into improved test plans, asset requirements, procedures, and recommendations for future scaling.

 Maintain a Safety First culture
 Follow all GM, DPG, AV Operations, AV Test Engineering, and applicable safety procedures and work controls.

 Verify that required personnel, training, vehicle qualifications, test equipment, track conditions, emergency support, communications, and approved procedures are in place before testing begins.

 Stop work and escalate when vehicle condition, system behavior, weather, track conditions, personnel readiness, facility conditions, or test setup creates unacceptable risk.

 Maintain the requirement that testing is conducted with appropriate onsite personnel and never rely on unsupported lone-person operations or unapproved after-hours activity.

 Support incident, near-miss, and abnormal-event documentation with accurate facts, timelines, evidence, and follow-up actions.

 Required qualifications
 Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, automotive, systems, computer, robotics, aerospace engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline.

 At least 3 years of relevant experience in autonomous vehicles, automotive engineering, robotics, aerospace, vehicle testing, systems integration, test engineering, or a related technical operations environment.

 Experience planning and executing vehicle, robotics, or other complex electro-mechanical system tests in a laboratory, proving-ground, field, or comparable operational environment.

 Experience troubleshooting software-enabled hardware systems using diagnostic information, logs, measurements, observations, and structured problem-solving methods.

 Ability to read and apply test procedures, requirements, acceptance criteria, operating instructions, and safety controls.

 Demonstrated ability to work independently, establish priorities, take initiative, and maintain ownership in an environment with limited onsite support.

 Ability to provide clear technical direction to operators, coordinators, contractors, or other support personnel during test execution without formal people-management responsibility.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including concise technical reporting, issue escalation, and remote collaboration across time zones and functions.

 Ability to work outdoors and in a proving-ground environment with exposure to heat, cold, dust, wind, sun, noise, vehicle traffic, and changing work conditions.

 Ability to perform hands-on vehicle readiness and troubleshooting activities, including inspecting vehicles, connecting or handling test equipment and data media, and moving through vehicle and track environments as required.

 Ability to work onsite at GM Desert Proving Ground in Yuma, Arizona, and travel approximately 10% as needed.

 Valid driver’s license and ability to meet applicable GM driver-training, vehicle-qualification, site-access, and safety requirements for closed-course vehicle testing.

 Preferred qualifications
 Direct experience testing autonomous vehicles, advanced driver-assistance systems, mobile robots, or other safety-critical autonomous systems.

 Experience with closed-course test execution, proving-ground operations, scripted scenario testing, release regression, feature validation, calibration support, or structured data collection.

 Experience owning a small test fleet or vehicle asset set, including vehicle readiness, configuration management, downtime recovery, maintenance coordination, and return-to-service decisions.

 Working knowledge of software-defined vehicle concepts, SDV 2.0 architecture, vehicle compute, electronic control units, over-the-air or branch-based software deployment, vehicle configuration, and software/hardware change management.

 Experience with automotive diagnostics, CAN or Ethernet-based vehicle networks, sensors, localization, calibration, time synchronization, data recording, connectivity, or AV system health monitoring.

 Familiarity with AV and vehicle tools such as Xray, INCA, Vehicle Spy, Notelogger, SC3 Debug App, Jumpstart, Launchpad, Starfleet, HAT, Drives, Webviz, Netradyne, Grafana, Looker, or comparable tools.

 Experience using Linux, command-line tools, Python, SQL, spreadsheets, or other methods to inspect logs, automate repetitive analysis, or improve test and fleet reporting.

 Experience directing small operational teams or contractors in a safety-critical, field, laboratory, proving-ground, or shift-based environment.

 Experience working at GM Desert Proving Ground, Yuma Proving Ground, Milford Proving Ground, or another proving ground with limited onsite technical support.

 Familiarity with formal issue-management, root-cause, change-control, safety-case, or corrective-action processes.

 Experience testing in variable weather, winter conditions, desert conditions, or other environments where facility and vehicle readiness directly affect test capacity.

The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of New York, Colorado, California, or Washington.

jobs.title: Controls Engineer
jobs.location: Arlington, Texas, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 DUTIES: Design, develop, and implement advanced controls and automation systems for automotive body shop manufacturing operations, ensuring system reliability, efficiency, and compliance with established engineering standards. Develop and document system requirements, functional specifications, and control strategies for automated manufacturing systems, including robotics, machine vision, and conveyance technologies. Program, configure, and troubleshoot Allen Bradley PLCs (including Safety Logic) and Siemens TIA Portal HMIs, ensuring seamless integration with plant wide automation systems. Design, implement, and maintain industrial communication networks—including EtherNet/IP, TCP/IP, and DeviceNet—to support real time communication across PLCs, robots, vision systems, and peripheral devices. Integrate, program, and optimize FANUC industrial robots for material handling, spot welding, dispensing, and vision guided operations. Develop, configure, and troubleshoot machine vision systems (Matrox, SICK, Keyence, Photoneo, FANUC Vision) for inspection, error proofing, and bin picking applications. Maintain and enhance vision guided bin picking solutions utilizing 3D vision technologies to increase automation efficiency and reduce manual handling. Support, maintain, and optimize conveyance systems, including Power & Free conveyors, Geo Pallet systems, skid conveyors, and Automated Guided Carts (AGCs), ensuring continuous and reliable production flow. Configure and troubleshoot Allen Bradley Variable Frequency Drives (PowerFlex, ArmorStart) and related motion control systems. Develop and implement error proofing systems such as torque verification (Atlas Copco), barcode readers (SICK, Matrox), RFID based tracking, and automated bin pick validation. Create and interpret electrical schematics using EPLAN to support system design, integration, commissioning, and troubleshooting. Perform root cause analysis of automation and controls failures using empirical data, trend analysis, diagnostic tools, and structured problem solving methodologies to drive corrective and preventive actions. Analyze manufacturing and operational data using DLA and Power BI (TBIA) to identify inefficiencies, improve throughput, and reduce downtime. Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, downtime elimination, and quality improvements (e.g., DRR reduction). Provide real time production support, including troubleshooting, maintenance assistance, and system optimization for high volume manufacturing lines. Develop and maintain custom engineering tools and applications to support automation systems, data analytics, and production performance monitoring. Ensure standardization, scalability, and reuse of automation components across new installations, upgrades, and major projects. Identify system vulnerabilities and implement 
 mitigation strategies to improve system reliability, robustness, and safety. Track, document, and report corrective actions, ensuring full closure and compliance with engineering and quality standards. Collaborate with cross functional partners—including manufacturing, quality, and maintenance—to support system integration, launch readiness, and production goals. Stay current with emerging technologies, industry trends, and best practices in industrial automation, robotics, and smart manufacturing. Hybrid Work Policy – 3 days In-Office, 2 Days Remote – Must be able to report to local office. 

REQUIREMENTS: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field of study and Two (2) years of experience as an Automation Engineer, Controls Engineer, or related occupation. Two (2) years of experience with the following: Designing, programming, and troubleshooting Allen Bradley PLCs, including Safety Logic; Developing and maintaining HMI systems; Designing and supporting industrial communication networks including EtherNet/IP, TCP/IP, and DeviceNet; Configuring and troubleshooting machine vision systems; Supporting and optimizing automated conveyance systems; Configuring and troubleshooting VFDs; and Implementing and supporting error proofing technologies. One (1) year of experience with the following: Programming and troubleshooting FANUC robots for material handling, spot welding, dispensing, and vision guided applications; Developing and supporting 3D vision–based bin picking systems; Supporting high volume manufacturing operations through troubleshooting, optimization, and downtime reduction; and Python and SQL.

Job Description 
 This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Warren, Michigan three times per week, at minimum 

 The Role 
 This position offers the opportunity to work in a highly collaborative team focused on propulsion related system models including thermal, hydraulic, lubrication and ventilation domains. Build 1D fluid dynamics & coarse 3D thermal models that directly impact design development, validation and eliminate hardware testing. Simulations include battery cell, battery pack, drive units, electric motors, power electronics, combustion engine and transmission related systems.

 Conceptualize, build, and exercise analytical system level models for electrified and conventional propulsion systems using 1D software tools (GT-SUITE, AMESIM, MATLAB, Simulink or similar)

 Own and advance analysis practices and/or tools to improve prediction fidelity and execution speed
 Collaborate with analysis counterparts across several VDDV teams representing global propulsion systems and vehicle engineering
 Mentor, train and lead our TCS India colleagues as well as new team members
 Provide technical leadership and problem resolution by leveraging analysis results
 Lead efficiency improvement projects, including the development of automation tools via Python or MATLAB
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor of Science in Engineering
 5+ years of experience with simulation, design, testing, or release of propulsion related systems
 1 year of experience with GT-SUITE, AMESIM or similar software
 Extensive experience with the principles of vehicle propulsion system design, operation, or testing
 ​

 Master of Science in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering with coursework in heat transfer or fluid mechanics 
 Extensive experience with test to model correlation processes, considering variation analysis
 Experience with programming or scripting in Python, MATLAB or similar software
 Extensive experience with Siemens NX CAD modeling. 
 Experience in AI / ML methods or Agentic workflows.

jobs.location: Milford, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Controls Software Engineer – Energy Source Control 

 Job Description: 

 Hybrid: This position does not require an employee to be on-site full-time to perform most effectively. The employee's role enables them to be onsite approximately 3 days per week.

 The Role:  
 Embedded Platform System & Infrastructure (EPSI) is a production level group that supports the definition, design, and development of all embedded controllers related to vehicle mechatronics. The Low Voltage Infrastructure (LVI) organization within EPSI is focused on the development of controls & diagnostic software centered around on-vehicle low voltage power generation, energy storage, power management, and distribution. This role is paramount to the successful review, development, simplification, integration and release of VIP and SDV2.0 architectures controller software. There is no better time to join this domain as we evolve to the next generation of low voltage power strategy, innovation, and capability for EVs, ICE and every product GM has to offer.
 We are seeking creative, highly motivated, agile thinkers with passion and expertise in embedded controls. The selected candidate will learn, modify existing and develop new innovative controls strategies, which will be at the core of all vehicles within the General Motors portfolio and essential to keeping General Motors at the forefront of low voltage related technologies.

 Responsibilities: 
 Lead development and implementation of controls development for complex low voltage related features in embedded C and C++. Proficiency in both is vital as this role will be centered around improvements, best practices institution, code efficiency, vulnerability surface mitigation and addressing feature to feature interference. Research and develop novel solutions to controls challenges.
 Contribute to ART Feature and user story elaboration into individual work items.  Contribute to ensuring that definition of done and acceptance criteria are well defined
 Provide information as required to calibration procedures 
 Ensure compliance to safety and governmental regulations while following GM-internal best practices
 Work cross-functionally with System Engineers, other Software Engineers, Architects, Calibrators, Scrum Managers and Scrum Leaders to ensure robust design
 Collaborate with other team members to define and integrate components, check functionality on the bench and in the vehicle
 Design and manage key strategic interfaces within deliverables to enable component reuse and consistency to standard methodologies
 Lead and support other specialists in root cause analysis and resolution of issues related to the low voltage electric power domain
 Verify functional performance of controls designs through testing (Unit, HIL, SIL, Vehicle), data analysis, and verification of acceptance criteria
 Document Intellectual Property
 Participate in the relevant team and program events: Program Increment Planning, DSU (Daily Stand Up), iteration reviews, ART inspection and adapt sessions etc.
 Build the capability of the team through mentorship, creation of training material, development of tools, etc.
 Identify opportunities and drive improvement initiatives through to completion for process, workflow, and strategic changes

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): 
 BS in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent degree.

Job Description 
 At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.   
   
 Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. 

 Role Type
Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to either the Milford Proving Grounds OR the Global Technical Center three (3) times per week, at minimum.
  
 The Role 
Join the innovative and high‑impact Planar Motion Coordination team within Global Systems Engineering, Safety, and Validation as a Senior System and System Safety Engineer. Our team defines and delivers the Vehicle Dynamics State Estimation and Vehicle Dynamics Motion Control systems that shape how every GM vehicle performs on the road.
 
In this multi-disciplined role, you will own the Vehicle Dynamics State Estimation (VDSE) System functional safety deliverables and support system design and requirement definition. VDSE is a foundational technology that fuses sensor data to calculate the vehicle’s dynamic state (reference velocity, accelerations, tire forces, and more), even in the presence of faults. This system enables a wide range of advanced control features across GM’s global portfolio. Your work will directly impact vehicle safety and support GM’s vision of Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, and Zero Congestion.
   
 What You’ll Do 
 ●      Lead the definition and completion of the VDSE system safety case for GM vehicle programs.
 ●      Define functional and performance requirements in collaboration with cross‑functional engineering and product teams.
 ●      Employ varied analysis techniques including hazard analysis, fault tree analysis, interface analysis, failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), and more.
 ●      Support execution of new requirements and cascading roll‑down to impacted organizations, ensuring alignment and traceability.
 ●      Guide confirmation of requirements through analysis, simulation, and physical testing (including HIL benches and vehicles).
 ●      Utilize model-based systems engineering techniques to improve traceability, design quality, and variant management.
 ●      Serve as the corporation’s subject matter expert for VDSE, influencing technology direction, integration strategies, and issue resolution.
 
What You’ll Need (Required Qualifications) 
 ●      Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics or related field of study.
 ●      5+ years of relevant engineering experience, ideally in systems engineering or functional safety.
 ●      Experience developing or integrating embedded control systems.
 ●      Familiarity with ISO 26262 or other functional safety standards such as IEC 61508, IEC 62304, or DO-178C.

We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard — from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. We hold our teams accountable for results and seek leaders who can influence teammates, stakeholders, and executives using data and logic.

This role involves identifying market opportunities, driving product vision, strategies, and roadmaps within the ADAS team’s broader objectives. You will play a key role in GM’s vision of a world with Zero Crashes and our transformation to industry leadership in software & services.

jobs.location: Markham, Ontario, Canada
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Job Description 
 Vacancy Status:  
 This posting is not for an existing vacancy within the organization and is open to new applications. (New Head Count) 

 AI Disclosure: 
 As part of the application process, Artificial Intelligence will be used in the hiring process for this role. 

 Work Arrangement  
 Hybrid: This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to Markham Elevation Centre (MEC) three times per week at minimum, or other frequency dictated by the business. 

 The Role: 
 
We are seeking a motivated software engineer to help verify and validate Propulsion Thermal Management functions across virtual, simulated, hardware-in-the-loop, and vehicle environments. In this role, you will translate system requirements and behavioral specifications into clear, traceable test cases, develop and execute automated system behavior tests, analyze results, and support the resolution of issues that affect vehicle software quality. 
 
The role is in the Vehicle Software and Electronics Engineering (VSEE) organization. The team is at the forefront of innovation, where vehicle software design, integration, release, and validation come together to improve engineering and quality processes. Your work will help ensure that thermal-management functions—including battery and propulsion-system temperature control, cabin conditioning, diagnostics, and degraded operating modes—perform as intended and support the delivery of high-quality GM vehicles. This work contributes to GM’s vision of a world with ZERO Crashes, ZERO Emissions, and ZERO Congestion. 

What You’ll do: 
 
 Translate Propulsion Thermal Management system requirements, system functions, and Behavioral Test Specifications (BTS) into clear, traceable system test cases, procedures, and acceptance criteria. Maintain linkage between requirements, test assets, execution results, and defects. 
 Develop, maintain, and execute automated System Behavior Tests (SBTs) and functional system tests for propulsion thermal functions across CoSim/SIL environments, with targeted validation on HIL benches and vehicles when real-time behavior, hardware I/O, or physical system response is required. 
 Validate end-to-end thermal-management behavior, including RESS/battery heating and cooling, power-electronics and drive-unit thermal protection, cabin heating and cooling, thermal request coordination and arbitration, sensor and actuator behavior, diagnostics, and degraded or remedial operating modes. 
 Support CoSim package readiness for Propulsion Thermal Management by checking package health, interfaces, configurations, virtual ECU behavior, plant-model connectivity, HWIO behavior, and environment sanity before broader regression or milestone testing. 
 Review automated regression results. Rapidly distinguish product/software defects from CoSim, plant-model, infrastructure, configuration, or test-script issues; perform initial root-cause isolation and route each issue to the appropriate owner. 
 Document failures with sufficient technical detail to reproduce the issue, including software and model versions, vehicle/environment conditions, calibrations or overrides, logs, expected versus actual behavior, and requirement/test-case references. Track defects through resolution and verify corrective actions through retest and regression. 
 Partner with Product System Engineers, System Owners, Functional System Architects, System/Sub-System Engineers, Software Quality Assurance Engineers, Software Integration Managers, calibration teams, and validation teams to define test scope, review BTS/STS content, resolve requirement ambiguity, and support TFRP milestone readiness. 
 Maintain test scripts, procedures, test data, dashboards, and supporting documentation for current software and CoSim releases. Share lessons learned, training materials, reusable test patterns, and best practices that improve consistency and reduce duplicated effort. 
 Participate in product, architecture, model, and test-environment reviews; provide actionable feedback on testability, observability, requirement quality, system boundaries, and end-to-end verification strategy. 
 
 Required Qualifications: 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
 Expected to graduate between December 2026 and June 2027. 
 Available to work full-time, 40 hours per week. 
 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Knowledge of vehicle thermal-management systems, including refrigeration cycles, refrigerant systems, HVAC, heat pumps, and associated controls
 Experience with automated testing frameworks, such as Robot Framework or Autobot, for system-level validation and regression testing. 
 Proficiency in programming or scripting using C, C++, Python, or comparable languages. 
 Familiarity with Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) processes and Gherkin syntax. 
 Experience using ETAS INCA, Intrepid Vehicle Spy, or similar data-acquisition and vehicle-network tools. 
 Experience with MATLAB and Simulink for plant-model development and integration; basic familiarity with simulation tools such as GT-Power, Amesim, or CarSim. 
 Familiarity with automotive communication technologies, including CAN, LIN, SPI, and automotive Ethernet. 
 Experience with virtualization, software integration, or virtual ECU environments. 
 Familiarity with visualization tools such as Power BI or Databricks dashboards to communicate technical insights effectively. 
 Familiarity with SQL and Databricks in an Azure Cloud environment. 
 Familiarity with data-storage solutions, databases, and data-processing frameworks. 
 Ability to translate business or engineering questions into data-driven solutions. 
 Experience developing or applying AI/ML-based solutions. 

Compensation:  
 The salary range for this role is $73,900 to $110,900. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.

jobs.title: Autonomous Vehicle Safety Case Technical Program Manager
jobs.location: 3 Locations
jobs.description:
Job Description 
 Why join us? 
At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard — from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale

 The Role 
 The Safety Assurance for Effective Autonomous Driving Software (SAFE-ADS) department is part of GM’s Global Product Safety, System, and Certification (GPSSC) organization. SAFE-ADS serves as a central body for automated driving system (ADS) safety assurance, bringing together technical expertise from across the company to support the safe development, testing, launch, and continuous improvement of advanced driving capabilities. 

 GM is seeking an Autonomous Vehicle Safety Case Technical Program Manager to lead the integrated execution of complex, cross-functional safety cases for ADS. This senior/staff individual contributor will bring structure, momentum, and transparency to the workstreams that support GM’s ADS safety case and safety assurance strategy. 
 The role will coordinate technical and operational work across safety case management, safety and risk management systems, operational safety and human factors, aggregate safety and rules-of-the-road metrics, counterfactual simulation, and related system-safety interfaces. The successful candidate will connect strategy to execution: translating safety objectives into actionable plans, aligning claims and sufficiency criteria with evidence and assessments, managing dependencies and risks, and driving decisions to closure across engineering, validation, operations, legal, public policy, and product teams. 

 This role is ideal for an experienced program leader who is comfortable operating in a technically complex, safety-critical environment; can synthesize diverse inputs into a coherent execution plan; and is motivated by the challenge of enabling the safe, measurable, and scalable deployment of ADS technology. 

 What You’ll Do  
 Integrated Program Leadership 
 Build and maintain integrated program plans covering safety case workstreams, milestones, dependencies, resource needs, risks, decisions, and deliverables. 
 Establish operating rhythms, governance forums, status reporting, action tracking, decision logs, and escalation paths that enable effective cross-functional execution. 
 Align safety case claims with ADS product, engineering, validation, operational, and launch milestones. 
 Translate evolving safety strategies and program objectives into clear workstream charters, measurable outcomes, delivery plans, and ownership models. 
 Identify schedule, scope, technical, evidence, resource, and cross-functional dependency risks; drive mitigation plans and escalate issues when needed. 
 Create clear, concise communications for technical teams, senior leaders, and cross-functional decision forums. 
 Safety Case and Assurance Execution 
 Coordinate the development, assessment, maintenance, and continuous improvement of ADS safety cases across product-launch contexts. 
 Drive alignment among safety claims, sufficiency criteria, evidence plans, assessment activities, and program milestones. 
 Establish and maintain traceability between safety strategies, claims, requirements, evidence, assessments, decisions, and changes in system scope or operating conditions. 
 Coordinate technical inputs from AI/ML, autonomy, systems engineering, functional safety, SOTIF, cybersecurity, software validation, simulation, human factors, operations, and product safety teams. 
 Track evidence readiness, assessment status, substantiation gaps, deviations, and corrective actions; ensure gaps are closed, actively managed, or supported by documented rationale. 
 Support impact assessments when the ADS, operational design domain, platform, release, feature behavior, or deployment plan changes. 
 Improve the processes, tools, and information flows used to manage the safety case and safety assurance lifecycle. 
 Continuous Improvement 
 Establish scalable methods for planning, prioritization, reporting, evidence management, and change control across SAFE-ADS. 
 Use program data and operational feedback to identify systemic issues, improve process health, and increase predictability of safety assurance delivery. 
 Promote early and frequent collaboration between safety assurance teams and the engineering and operations organizations developing and deploying ADS capabilities. 
 Help mature GM’s safety assurance practices as ADS technology, operating scope, evidence methods, and industry expectations evolve. 
 
 Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, systems engineering, robotics, safety engineering, mathematics, or a related technical field. 
 7+ years of experience leading complex technical programs in autonomous vehicles, ADAS, software-intensive systems, systems engineering, product safety, safety assurance, or another safety-critical domain. 
 Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional programs with multiple workstreams, stakeholders, dependencies, and enterprise-level visibility. 
 Strong program management capabilities, including integrated planning, milestone management, dependency tracking, risk management, governance, issue resolution, and executive communication. 
 Experience translating ambiguous technical or safety objectives into structured execution plans, measurable outcomes, and clear ownership. 
 Experience developing, supporting, assessing, or managing safety cases, assurance cases, safety arguments, or equivalent evidence-based safety programs. 
 Working knowledge of safety assurance concepts and practices, including requirements traceability, evidence management, hazard or risk management, change control, and assessment processes. 
 Ability to understand and connect technical work across software, AI/ML, systems engineering, validation, simulation, human factors, operations, and product safety. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor information for technical, operational, and executive audiences. 
 Ability to influence without authority, build alignment across functions, work through ambiguity, and drive action to closure. 
 Passion for autonomous vehicle technology and safe deployment of advanced driving capabilities. 
 
 What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) 
 Advanced degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, systems engineering, safety management, mathematics, or a related field.

Job Description 
 The Team: 
 The Programming, EIO/HWIO (Ethernet Input/Output Hardware Input/Output) Systems Engineering Team represents two of the eight Mech Infra Systems teams: the Mech Infra Programming System and the Controller Hardware System (EIO/HWIO); the other six are Diagnostics, Ethernet Communications, Non-Ethernet Communications, Power Management, Safety, and Cybersecurity. The Programming System owns the end-to-end strategy, requirements, flows, test automation, and recovery behavior that enable SDV ECUs to be safely, securely, and repeatably programmed and updated across development, manufacturing, service, and field environments. 

 The EIO/HWIO System defines and validates controller input/output capabilities—including sensing, actuation, diagnostics, I/O mapping, performance, and voltage-reference monitoring—to ensure controllers and Ethernet I/O devices operate reliably and are diagnosable. Together, these two systems represent complementary areas of Mech Infra SW: Programming manages how software is delivered and updated, while EIO/HWIO enables the controller-level interfaces through which the system interacts with physical devices. Programming also supports any previous electrical architectures such as VIP.
